segments.prompt:
Picture 1 is the young man carrying the worn poetry book. Picture 2 is the night-only secondhand bookstore, shelves crowded with old books under a warm desk lamp. Picture 3 is the worn poetry book itself, its cloth cover softened with age.

shots:
[Shot 1] Wide shot, Tracking Shot — the camera follows <Picture 1> as he pushes open the door of <Picture 2>, a small bell chiming, his footsteps slowing among towering stacks of old books, <Picture 3> held close against his chest.
[Shot 2] Medium shot, Push In — slowly moving closer on <Picture 1>'s face as he asks in a low, testing tone, <Picture 3> still cradled in one arm: "还开着吗？我想卖一本书。"

ambience: A faint bell chime fades under the low hum of the night, pages rustling somewhere in the stacks; no music.

Picture 1 is the woman who owns the bookstore, composed, in her fifties. Picture 2 is the worn poetry book with a faded cloth cover and a handwritten inscription on its title page.

shots:
[Shot 1] Medium shot, Pan Left — the camera pans to <Picture 1> as she looks up from behind a stack of ledgers, sets down her pen, and lifts a hand toward the counter, wordlessly asking for <Picture 2>.
[Shot 2] Close-up, Push In — pushing in on <Picture 1>'s fingers as they open <Picture 2> to its title page, stopping on a line of handwriting, held there without turning the page.

ambience: The lamp hums faintly, a page turns somewhere else in the stacks, then everything goes still around her held breath; no music.

Picture 1 is the young man who has just sold the worn poetry book; the book remains on the counter. Picture 2 is the woman who owns the bookstore, composed, in her fifties.

shots:
[Shot 1] Medium shot, Static Shot — holding steady on <Picture 1> as he studies her stillness and asks, uncertain: "老板？书有问题吗？"
[Shot 2] Close-up, Push In — pushing in on <Picture 2>'s face, carefully composed, as she answers without looking up: "没有。这本我要了，给你双倍。"

ambience: The shop stays quiet around her measured voice, only the faint hum of the lamp and the distant creak of an old floorboard; no music.

Picture 1 is the young man who has just sold the worn poetry book. Picture 2 is the woman who owns the bookstore, composed, in her fifties. Picture 3 is the worn poetry book with a faded cloth cover.

shots:
[Shot 1] Wide shot, Pan Right — following <Picture 1> as he takes his payment and turns for the door empty-handed, leaving the book on the counter, the small bell chiming once as he steps out into the dark.
[Shot 2] Close-up, Static Shot — a folded note slips from between the pages of <Picture 3> as <Picture 2> reopens it alone at the counter, drifting down to rest by her feet.
[Shot 3] Close-up, Pull Out — <Picture 2> bends down to pick up the note and unfolds it, the handwritten inscription "致晚晚" catching the lamplight. She says quietly to herself: "晚晚，这是姐姐当年写给你的。" The frame pulls back to hold her alone in the quiet shop; the sister remains absent.

ambience: The bell's last chime fades into the hush of the empty shop, paper rustling once as the note unfolds; no music, just the held quiet of a room that has just recognized something.

episodes.opening: 深夜旧书店快打烊时，周亦抱着一本卷边诗集进门，询问能否卖书。

ending.event: 陈叙在周亦离开后拾起书中滑落的字条，认出自己写给妹妹的「致晚晚」，独自留在书店灯下。
